notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached and no hardware backend was run. No deviation from the card: the family-config decision and the MujocoDriver helper express the model. The card lists no entry_symbols, so there was no symbol to verify; the card's five model files exist in the clone. The package serves the card's first model, agilex_piper/scene.xml (models[0]), as a simulated R0 world.sim: the step action is data.ctrl, bounded per actuator by the model's actuator_ctrlrange (seven position actuators; the piper position default inherits the joint range with inheritrange=1), and cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults. The other card models are not served by this package; changing model_path and facts serves another one. MuJoCo was not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so the fake backend (fake.py) is a stand-in mujoco module: it parses the MJCF (scene.xml includes piper.xml) for the joint count, actuator count and control ranges, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion and resolves no mesh, contact, equality or tendon constraint; it was never compared with the real engine. The sim path (a backend that backends does not name, which imports the real mujoco) was not run. Expected warnings are G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (the fake backend is the stand-in library, not the upstream simulator, so native calls are not recorded and G7 has no fake surface to check) and G8.NO_UNIT x3 (the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl and seed). No catalogue requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. There are no operator-required limits, so no site-limits.example.json is needed. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
